bank_name: Engineers Day 2026 Debugging Arena - Java Problem Bank

problems.title: Sum of Even Numbers
problems.problem_statement: Read N integers and print the sum of all even numbers.
problems.input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers.
problems.output_format: Print the sum of all even integers.

bugs.description: The condition selects odd numbers instead of even numbers.
bugs.why_wrong: An even number has remainder 0 when divided by 2.

problems.title: Largest of Three
problems.problem_statement: Read three integers and print the largest value.

bugs.description: The program replaces largest when c is smaller instead of when c is larger.
bugs.why_wrong: To find the largest value, c must replace largest only when c > largest.

problems.title: Simple Interest
problems.problem_statement: Calculate simple interest using principal P, rate R, and time T. Use SI = P * R * T / 100.
problems.input_format: Three numbers: principal, rate, and time.
problems.output_format: Print the simple interest with two decimal places.

bugs.description: The percentage calculation divides by 10 instead of 100.
bugs.why_wrong: A percentage rate must be converted from percent by dividing by 100.

problems.title: Print Countdown
problems.problem_statement: Read N and print all integers from N down to 1, separated by spaces.
problems.output_format: Print N, N-1, ..., 1 separated by spaces.

bugs.description: The loop stops when i becomes 1, so 1 is never printed.
bugs.why_wrong: The required countdown includes 1, so the loop condition must allow i == 1.

problems.title: Count Digits Greater Than Five
problems.problem_statement: Read a non-negative integer and count how many of its digits are greater than 5.
problems.output_format: Print the number of digits greater than 5.

bugs.description: The condition counts digits equal to 5 even though only digits greater than 5 should be counted.
bugs.why_wrong: The condition must be digit > 5.

problems.title: First Occurrence in an Array
problems.problem_statement: Read N integers and a target. Print the zero-based index of the first occurrence of the target, or -1 if it is absent.
problems.input_format: First line contains N. Second line contains N integers. Third line contains the target.
problems.output_format: Print the first zero-based index or -1.

bugs.description: The search continues after finding a match and overwrites the answer when the target appears again.
bugs.why_wrong: The problem asks for the first occurrence, so the loop must stop after the first match.

problems.title: Reverse a String
problems.problem_statement: Read a word and print its characters in reverse order.

bugs.description: The loop runs forward and excludes the last character instead of traversing from the last character to the first.
bugs.why_wrong: To reverse the word, characters must be appended starting at index length-1 and moving down to 0.

problems.title: Row Sum of a Matrix
problems.problem_statement: Read an R x C matrix and print the sum of each row on a separate line.
problems.input_format: First line contains R and C, followed by R rows containing C integers.
problems.output_format: Print R row sums, one per line.

bugs.description: The inner loop stops at c - 1, so the last element of every row is skipped.
bugs.why_wrong: Every column from 0 through c-1 must be included in the row sum.

problems.title: Student Result Calculator
problems.problem_statement: Read marks for five subjects. Print total, average to two decimal places, and PASS or FAIL. A student passes only if every subject mark is at least 40.
problems.input_format: One line containing five integer marks.
problems.output_format: Print total, average, and PASS or FAIL on separate lines.

bugs.description: The subject pass threshold is 35 instead of 40.
bugs.why_wrong: Every subject must have at least 40 marks.

bugs.description: The average is divided by 4 instead of 5.
bugs.why_wrong: There are five subjects.

bugs.description: The program sets passed to true when the average is at least 40, even if a subject has failed.
bugs.why_wrong: Passing requires every subject to meet the minimum, not merely a sufficient average.

bugs.description: The passing output is PASSED instead of PASS.
bugs.why_wrong: The required output is exactly PASS or FAIL.

problems.title: Shopping Bill
problems.problem_statement: Read the prices of three items. Calculate subtotal, discount, and final bill. If subtotal is at least 2000, give a 10% discount; otherwise give a 5% discount. Add a fixed delivery charge of 50 after the discount. Print subtotal, discount, and final bill with two decimal places.
problems.output_format: Print subtotal, discount, and final bill on separate lines.

bugs.description: The discount rates are reversed: 5% is used for subtotals of at least 2000.
bugs.why_wrong: The higher 10% discount applies when subtotal is at least 2000.

bugs.description: The lower-tier discount is 10% instead of 5%.
bugs.why_wrong: Subtotals below 2000 receive a 5% discount.

bugs.description: The delivery charge is subtracted from the bill.
bugs.why_wrong: The fixed delivery charge is added after applying the discount.

bugs.description: The final bill subtracts the delivery charge instead of adding it.
bugs.why_wrong: A delivery charge increases the amount the customer pays.

problems.title: Electricity Bill
problems.problem_statement: Calculate an electricity bill. The first 100 units cost 2 per unit, the next 100 units cost 3 per unit, and every unit above 200 costs 5 per unit. Add a fixed charge of 50.

bugs.description: The first 100 units are charged at 3 instead of 2 per unit.
bugs.why_wrong: The first slab rate is 2 per unit.

bugs.description: The second slab is charged at 2 instead of 3 per unit.
bugs.why_wrong: Units 101 through 200 cost 3 per unit.

bugs.description: Units above 200 are charged at 4 instead of 5 per unit.
bugs.why_wrong: Every unit above 200 costs 5.

bugs.description: The fixed charge is 40 instead of 50.
bugs.why_wrong: The specified fixed charge is 50.

problems.title: Attendance Eligibility
problems.problem_statement: Read the total number of classes and the number attended by a student. Calculate attendance percentage. A student is eligible if attendance is at least 75%. Also print the number of classes missed.
problems.input_format: Two integers: total classes and attended classes.
problems.output_format: Print attendance percentage to two decimal places, number of missed classes, and ELIGIBLE or NOT ELIGIBLE on separate lines.

bugs.description: Integer division occurs before multiplying by 100.
bugs.why_wrong: Both operands are integers, so the decimal portion is lost before the percentage is calculated.

bugs.description: The eligibility condition uses > 75 instead of >= 75.
bugs.why_wrong: Exactly 75% attendance is eligible.

bugs.description: The NOT ELIGIBLE case prints ELIGIBLE.
bugs.why_wrong: The else branch represents attendance below the required threshold.

bugs.description: The percentage is printed with one decimal place instead of two.
bugs.why_wrong: The required output format specifies two digits after the decimal point.
